Spectrum Challenge-001 (precursor m/z 222.023).
Selected top-1: Cc1ccc2c(n1)cccc2S(=O)(=O)O (confidence: medium).
Justification: Candidate 0 (2-Methyl-5-quinolinesulfonic acid) has the highest MS-CLIP score (0.812) and the highest CFM-ID cosine vs experimental (0.6903) among all candidates. Critically, CFM-ID predicted a peak at m/z 142.0662 for candidate 0, which corresponds to loss of SO3 (79.957 Da) from the precursor at 222.023, consistent with the observed fragment at m/z 158.0611 (loss of ~63.96, i.e. SO2+O or HSO3 rearrangement) and the quinoline ring system retaining the methyl group. The experimental peak at m/z 158.0611 is best rationalized by candidate 0's quinoline-methyl scaffold, where SO3 loss from the sulfonate is a well-known fragmentation pathway for arylsulfonic acids in negative mode.
Peak-level claims:
  - m/z 158.0611 corresponds to loss of SO3 (79.957 Da) from [M-H]- precursor at 222.023, yielding the deprotonated methylquinoline fragment
  - m/z 131.0502 corresponds to further loss of CO (27.995 Da) from the m/z 158.0611 fragment, arising from ring-opening rearrangement
  - m/z 107.0491 corresponds to loss of C2H2 (26.016 Da) from m/z 131.0502, fragment of the quinoline core
  - m/z 157.0533 corresponds to loss of H from m/z 158.0611, arises from radical stabilization of the methylquinolinyl anion

Spectrum Challenge-204 (precursor m/z 369.125).
Selected top-1: Cc1ccccc1OP(=O)(Oc2ccccc2C)Oc3ccccc3C (confidence: medium).
Justification: Candidate 0 (Tris(2-methylphenyl) phosphate) has the highest MS-CLIP score (0.735) and its CFM-ID predicted spectrum (cosine 0.6432) directly reproduces the key experimental peaks at m/z 65.0386, 91.0542, 261.0675, and 369.125, all of which appear in the top experimental peaks. The ortho-methyl substitution pattern is consistent with the observed m/z 261.0676 fragment (loss of one 2-methylphenoxy group from [M+H]+, 369.125 − 108.058 = 261.067), which is absent or weaker in para/meta isomers whose CFM-ID cosines are slightly lower (0.6626, 0.6562). Candidates 3 and 4 (propyl/isopropyl variants) score substantially lower in CFM-ID cosine (0.4565, 0.3773), ruling them out.
Peak-level claims:
  - m/z 261.0676 corresponds to loss of 2-methylphenol (C7H8O, 108.058) from [M+H]+ at 369.125, yielding the [M+H−C7H8O]+ phosphate fragment
  - m/z 91.0542 corresponds to fragment of tropylium/methylenecyclohexadienyl cation (C7H7+) from 2-methylphenyl group
  - m/z 165.0699 corresponds to loss of two 2-methylphenoxy groups leaving a methylphenyl-phosphate oxocarbenium fragment
  - m/z 65.0387 corresponds to fragment of cyclopentadienyl cation (C5H5+) arising from retro-Diels-Alder of the tropylium ion at 91.054

Selected top-1: C=CCCCCOC(=O)c1ccccc1C(=O)OCCCCC=C (confidence: high).
Justification: Candidate 0 (Di-5-hexen-1-yl phthalate) has the highest CFM-ID cosine of 0.4615 and its predicted top peaks reproduce the dominant experimental ions at m/z 149.0233, 231.1016, 331.1904, 83.0855, and 55.0542 essentially exactly, including the characteristic phthalate protonated anhydride at 149.0233 (C8H5O3+).
